Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
1105 PM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

...New DISCUSSION, MARINE...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Seasonably hot with highs in the 90s and heat index values
  100-107F each day.
  
- An isolated late day shower can't be ruled out along the
  seabreeze in the afternoons.
  
- Slightly better rain chances expected Thursday into early next
  week for the eastern and southern parts of the region as some 
  deeper moisture flows back inland. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1105 PM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

Ridging centered over the Southwest CONUS/Four Corners will keep 
uneventful weather over the region through the better half of next 
week at least. Heights and 850mb temperatures are still expected to 
drop into the weekend, resulting slightly lower heat stress and 
surface temperatures. Reduced subsidence and rising PWs should bring 
better rain chances during this period as well, with isolated to 
scattered showers and storms possible along the seabreeze/baybreeze 
each afternoon. Highs remain in the 90s each day with heat indices 
reaching the triple digits in the afternoon. Some patchy fog will be 
possible during the early morning hours.

03

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 635 PM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

VFR conditions are expected for much of the forecast period, with
the exemption of the potential for a brief period of MVFR cigs to
possibly IFR cigs from around 11-14Z for some sites. Winds will 
relax to 5 KTS or less tonight and become VRB. Winds will be SSW 
at 5-10 KTS Thu morning and turn S-SE at 08-12 KTS Thu afternoon.
There is a slight chance for iso showers/thunderstorms in the
afternoon, in particular for HOU/IAH/SGR/CXO. Storms, is any, are
expected to dissipate in the evening. 

Cotto 

&&

Onshore winds 10-15 knots and seas of 2-4 feet are expected 
throughout the next several days. Rain chances increase slightly 
through early next week. Chances for isolated to scattered showers 
and storms will be greatest during the late night through early 
afternoon hours for the Gulf.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
638 PM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- A typical summer weather pattern will prevail through this week
  with a few afternoon thunderstorms each day. 

- Afternoon highs will climb into the low to mid 90s each day 
  with maximum heat indices ranging from 101 to 109.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(This afternoon through next Tuesday)
Issued at 1122 AM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

Typical summer pattern looks to continue through our day-to-day 
forecast with little change expected. Upper level ridging is 
currently centered over New Mexico and a weak upper level trough 
situated in the eastern Gulf is leading to very weak upper level 
flow over our area. Diurnally driven showers will persist daily 
over sections of our area. Weak upper level flow will lead to slow
moving storms, but the average PWAT values dampen the chances for
flooding rainfall. 

A surface high pressure is situated over the eastern Gulf is
bringing light southerly winds over our area. Currently sporadic 
storms have began to initiate over much of the region. Outflow 
boundaries and cloud shading will likely keep heat indices from 
reaching the values required for a heat advisory. Modest DCAPE 
values suggest a small chance for localized strong downdrafts in 
convection through this afternoon.

Soileau

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 626 PM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

Convection across the area will gradually decrease with the loss
of heating over the next couple of hours. Looks like KLCH and KAEX
will be the only terminals that may have any impacts from the
convection. After sunset, conditions will stabilize with mainly
VFR conditions. The only caveat is the potential for some patchy
light fog with MVFR conditions around sunrise. 

On Thursday, more afternoon convection is expected so will mention
VCTS at all terminals after 06/18z.

07/Rua

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1122 AM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

Onshore winds are forecast to be 5-8 kts with gusts over 10 kts
possible. Isolated pulse storms are possible in the afternoons
with greater coverage closer to the coast.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1122 AM CDT Wed Aug 5 2026

KBDI values continue to climb. Isolated showers and thunderstorms
are expected each afternoon will provide local relief but 
otherwise no widespread rain is expected. Minimum RH values will
be around 50%.
